newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Bank to raise deposit rates.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Bank to raise deposit rates.

text.p: Bangkok Bank Plc said on Friday it will raise its deposit rates by about 25 basis points soon in a bid to halt its falling market share of domestic funds.
Bangkok Bank executive vice chairman Piti Sithi-amnuai said: "We would definitely raise deposit rates soon...within a few weeks at the most."
He declined to say if the planned hike would be made across the board.
Piti said Bangkok Bank, Thailand's biggest commercial bank, has no immediate plan to raise its lending rates but may be required to do so over time to accommodate its future higher funding cost.
Bangkok Bank currently offers clients 9.00-10.00 percent annual interest for three-month fixed deposits.
Market analysts said Bangkok Bank's planned deposit rate hike would prompt other Thai banks to follow suit.

Piti said medium and small Thai commercial banks have been more aggressive than his bank in gaining bigger market shares in deposits over the past year, at the expense of his bank which analysts estimate enjoys about 24 percent share of total Thai bank deposits.
"Whatever Bangkok Bank decides will have a knock-on effect on other Thai banks. It will narrow the average interest rate spread for the whole industry," a foreign analyst at a finance company said.
He said Siam Commercial Bank Plc, one of the top four Thai banks, has seen its deposit market share grow in the past two years because of its fine-tuned marketing strategy.
